description: Generate a source-linked report on your federal representatives from your address, personalized by angle/tone/depth.
author: @destin
tagline: Know your federal reps, tailored to what you care about.
longDescription:
Drop in your address and Claude generates a personalized briefing on every federal official who represents you — President, VP, both U.S. Senators, and your House Rep — with state-level officials included as named stubs. Pick the angle you care about (housing, climate, immigration, foreign policy, or anything you type), choose a tone (neutral, critical, positive, civic, friendly, deep-research), and decide whether you want the full eight-section report per rep or a custom subset.

Every factual claim in the output is footnoted with a source URL you can click through to verify, and reports are saved to your Encyclopedia by default so you can reread them before voting, calling an office, or writing a letter. The first-time setup runs a one-line interactive prompt to capture an API key for the data source; everything after that is just conversation.

description: Build and share custom themes — AI-generated or from scratch
author: @destin
tagline: Make the app look like you.
longDescription:
The `/theme-builder` skill — describe a vibe, drop in a wallpaper, or write a detailed brief, and Claude generates three full YouCoded theme concepts in a side-by-side browser preview. Pick one and you land on a single-page kit refiner where palette, chrome, bubbles, fonts, effects, wallpaper, mascots, and icons are all swappable columns; iterate until it feels like you, then build the pack and the app hot-reloads with your new look.

Finished themes are real YouCoded theme packs (manifest + assets + custom CSS) you can install locally, share with friends via QR/link, or publish to the community theme registry where they get an auto-generated preview PNG. The skill enforces the 15 required theme tokens and runs contrast validation on the way out, so anything you publish is guaranteed legible.

description: Search your past conversations — find what you worked on and whether it got finished.
author: @destin
tagline: Find that thing you half-remember working on.
longDescription: Searches every past YouCoded and Claude Code conversation on this device by what you actually typed, then points you at the one that matters. Answers "did we ever finish that?" without reopening a dozen sessions.

description: Foundation toolkit — safety hooks, commands, sync infrastructure, diagnostics
author: @destin
tagline: Bundled plugin — hooks and setup skills. Being deprecated.
longDescription:
`youcoded-core` is a bundled YouCoded plugin that ships with the app. It contributes a small number of safety hooks (write-guard, worktree-guard), a session-start hook, and two first-run helper skills (`setup-wizard`, `remote-setup`). It's auto-installed at `~/.claude/plugins/youcoded-core/` so most users never touch it directly.

**Heads up — this plugin is being deprecated.** `write-guard` is moving into the app natively, the remaining helpers are being folded in or retired, and the repo will eventually be archived. Existing installs keep working; new capabilities are landing in the app itself or in dedicated marketplace plugins (`youcoded-encyclopedia`, `youcoded-inbox`, `wecoded-themes-plugin`, etc.) rather than here.

description: Personal knowledge system — journaling, encyclopedia, interviewer, librarian, compiler
author: @destin
tagline: Your life, written down and searchable.
longDescription:
Your life, written down once and reachable forever. The Encyclopedia bundle is four skills working together: `journaling-assistant` runs a daily check-in that prompts you through the parts of your day worth remembering; `encyclopedia-update` routes new journal content into eight modular source files (people, places, beliefs, goals, work, etc.); `encyclopedia-interviewer` proactively notices gaps and runs targeted interviews to fill them; and `encyclopedia-librarian` produces purpose-built briefings — "prep me for tomorrow's meeting with X", "review my last six months", "pull together everything I've said about Y".

The whole system is plain markdown stored locally in `~/.claude/encyclopedia/` — you own every word, you can read and edit it in any text editor, and sync it across devices via the YouCoded app's built-in sync (Settings → Sync). Four detail levels (Full, Personal, Professional, Public) let you control how much intimate context appears in any given output, so the same encyclopedia can power both deeply personal reflection and cleanly shareable professional summaries.

description: Fork-file: track recipes, meals, and food preferences
author: @destin
longDescription:
A two-part food tracker with personality. The first part keeps a live inventory of what's actually in your pantry, fridge, and freezer — log a grocery run by texting Claude a receipt or a fridge photo, ask "what do I have for dinner?", and get age/freshness warnings on items getting old. The second part tracks fast food spending and ordering patterns by restaurant and item, so you can see how much that DoorDash habit is actually costing you.

Claude addresses you with rotating affectionate-roast nicknames (Fatty, Chonk, Sir Eats-a-Lot…) and the teasing escalates with the size of the order — light ribbing for a $30 grocery run, full grief for a $14 fast food trip for one. Data lives in two CSVs under `~/.claude/fork-file/` so you can always export, edit, or back it up yourself. Built on `fork-file` underneath; install this bundle for the full UX.

description: Process notes and screenshots from Todoist, Drive, Gmail, and more
author: @destin
tagline: Triage captured notes into something useful.
longDescription:
Pulls items from every inbox you actually use — Todoist tasks, Google Drive notes, Gmail, Apple Notes, Apple Reminders, iCloud Drive, even local screenshots dropped in a staging folder — and triages them in one conversation. Claude isn't just routing items; it actively *resolves* them: answering questions, applying feedback, creating tasks, deleting noise, filing screenshots into your journal or encyclopedia.

Provider-agnostic by design — pick the sources you actually use during setup, leave the rest off. The session-start hook quietly counts unprocessed items and surfaces a reminder when there's something to look at, so you never have to remember to open your inbox; it comes to you. Works hand-in-glove with `youcoded-encyclopedia` (journal entries get filed) and the YouCoded app's built-in sync (multi-device captures all flow into one queue).

description: Send and read SMS/iMessage via MCP servers
author: @destin
longDescription:
Send and read SMS and iMessage from inside Claude. Drafts replies in your voice, sends from the phone number bridged through the configured MCP server, and surfaces incoming messages so Claude can react to them in your normal chat session. Useful for catching up on a thread without picking up your phone, or for asking Claude to draft something tricky and then send it for you.

The heavy lifting is in the bundled MCP servers — `gmessages` for Android/Google Messages, `imessage` for macOS — both of which the plugin will configure during install. Pairs naturally with `youcoded-inbox` for inbound triage, and with `youcoded-encyclopedia`'s deep-search mode for "go find that thing I texted Mom about in October" queries.

description: Tone presets — casual, conversational, academic, professional
author: @destin
tagline: Match Claude's tone to the task.
longDescription:
A small library of tone presets for Claude — `casual`, `conversational`, `academic`, and `professional` — that you can flip between with a single command depending on what you're doing. Use `casual` for chat with friends, `academic` for paper drafts and lit-review summaries, `professional` for emails and proposals, `conversational` for blog posts and personal essays.

Each style is a plain markdown file under `styles/` describing the voice rules (formality, structure, vocabulary, hedging) so the presets are inspectable and forkable — copy one, tweak it, and now you have your own. No model switching, no settings menu — just type the name and Claude takes on the voice for the rest of the conversation.
